boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Massachusetts-Lowell, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key first-weekend sequence that starts on campus and extends into Lowell’s public history sites.

cards.title: Start at University Crossing
cards.subtitle: Campus student center
cards.notes: Use the student center as a first meetup point, then check its event listings or ask staff where student activities are gathering.
cards.short_summary: A central campus stop for meeting up and finding programmed events.
cards.evidence_claim: University Crossing maintains an events page and manages events occurring in the building.
cards.source_title: Events at University Crossing | UMass Lowell
cards.access_notes: Check the building’s event listing and any event-specific access requirements.

cards.title: Set a study-home base at Lydon
cards.subtitle: North Campus library
cards.notes: Walk through Lydon to locate its quiet and group study areas; save a spot for a short reset between campus activities.
cards.short_summary: A North Campus library stop with quiet and collaborative study space.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Lowell identifies Lydon Library on North Campus as providing group and quiet study space.
cards.source_title: Welcome Back from UML Library | UMass Lowell
cards.access_notes: Library access and hours can vary by term; confirm current hours before visiting.

cards.title: See what’s happening at Club Hub
cards.subtitle: University Crossing
cards.notes: Stop by Club Hub and look for student-organization activity, then use UML Engage to follow up on clubs that match your interests.
cards.short_summary: A University Crossing destination for connecting with student organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Lowell directs students to stop by the Club Hub in University Crossing and notes that UML Engage can be used to search for clubs.
cards.source_title: Join a Student Club or Organization | UMass Lowell
cards.access_notes: Student group meetings and events may have their own schedules or entry requirements.

cards.title: Move around at the Campus Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 322 Aiken St., East Campus
cards.notes: Bring your UCARD, take a quick lap through the facility, and check the court calendar for open recreation before choosing an activity.
cards.short_summary: A large East Campus recreation facility with fitness, track, and multipurpose courts.
cards.evidence_claim: The Campus Recreation Center has fitness areas, an indoor track, and courts used for basketball, pickleball, volleyball, and badminton.
cards.access_notes: Full-time UML students have access at no additional cost; use a valid UCARD and check current facility hours.

cards.entity_name: UMass Lowell Bellegarde Boathouse and Kayak Center
cards.title: Check out the riverside Kayak Center
cards.subtitle: 500 Pawtucket Boulevard
cards.notes: Visit during posted open hours to orient yourself to the riverfront facility and ask staff about rentals, instruction, tours, or shuttle options.
cards.short_summary: A university kayak facility on Pawtucket Boulevard.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Lowell lists the Bellegarde Boathouse and Kayak Center at 500 Pawtucket Boulevard and offers rentals, programs, tours, and instruction.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Kayak Center | UMass Lowell
cards.access_notes: Seasonal hours apply; review the Kayak Center’s current schedule and any rental or waiver requirements.

cards.title: Find the South Campus library
cards.subtitle: South Campus
cards.notes: Use O’Leary for a quieter afternoon pause, or scan the study-room QR codes if your new group wants a place to plan together.
cards.short_summary: A South Campus library with quiet and group study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: UMass Lowell identifies O’Leary Library on South Campus as providing group and quiet study space and describes QR-code room reservations.
cards.source_title: Welcome Back from UML Library | UMass Lowell
cards.access_notes: Library access and hours can vary by term; confirm current hours before visiting.

cards.title: Look for Hands-On History
cards.subtitle: 115 John St., Lowell National Historical Park
cards.notes: If your weekend matches the second Saturday, drop in for the listed Hands-On History session and confirm the current activity on the center calendar.
cards.short_summary: A UMass Lowell–National Park Service partnership offering recurring hands-on history programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Tsongas Industrial History Center lists free, no-registration Hands-On History drop-in events on the second Saturday of each month from 1 to 4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Events and Programs | Family Programs | UMass Lowell
cards.access_notes: This activity is scheduled for the second Saturday of each month; confirm the date and program details before going.

cards.entity_name: Lowell National Historical Park Visitor Center
cards.title: Get oriented at the park visitor center
cards.subtitle: 246 Market St., downtown Lowell
cards.notes: Pick up park information, ask a ranger about exhibits and tours, and use the stop to shape the rest of your downtown walk.
cards.short_summary: A downtown orientation point for Lowell National Historical Park sites and programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lowell National Historical Park Visitor Center at 246 Market Street provides information about park exhibits, guided tours, and special events.
cards.source_title: Visitor Center | Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: The National Park Service lists daily seasonal hours; check the current operating-hours page before visiting.

cards.title: Explore the Mogan Cultural Center
cards.subtitle: 40 French St., downtown Lowell
cards.notes: Walk through the two exhibits and give yourself time to compare the boarding-house recreation with the city’s wider cultural-history display.
cards.short_summary: A free cultural-history stop inside a historic Lowell boarding house.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mogan Cultural Center at 40 French Street contains the Into an 1840s Boarding House and One City, Many Cultures exhibits, with free admission.
cards.source_title: Places To Go | Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Observe posted hours; the National Park Service lists seasonal operating times for this location.

cards.title: Finish with a daytime canal walk
cards.subtitle: Lowell National Historical Park canal district
cards.notes: Take a daylight walk along the canal, follow posted conditions, and leave bikes, skateboards, and roller skates off the walkway.
cards.short_summary: A pedestrian canal route connecting historic park areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Lowell National Historical Park identifies the Northern Canal Walkway as a pedestrian area and prohibits bicycles, skateboards, and roller skates there.
cards.source_title: Superintendent’s Compendium | Lowell National Historical Park
cards.access_notes: Use in daylight and follow posted closures; the route closes seasonally from School Street Bridge to Pawtucket Street Bridge.
